title: Coskeleton comparison under a local matching surjection
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, let $n\geq1$, and let $f:L\to K$ be a morphism of simplicial presheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Assume $L_i\to K_i$ is an isomorphism for $i<n$, $L_n\to K_n$ becomes surjective after sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and both $L$ and $K$ are $n$-coskeletal (the canonical morphisms $L\to\operatorname{cosk}_n\operatorname{sk}_nL$ and $K\to\operatorname{cosk}_n\operatorname{sk}_nK$ of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton] are isomorphisms). Then for any commutative ring $R$, $f$ induces an isomorphism on every homology sheaf of the alternating-face complexes of free $R$-module sheaves on $L$ and $K$.

source.place: Hypercoverings, Lemma Tag 01GD (label lemma-acyclicity), lines 662-715. Proof route: replace K_n by the image of L_n and coskeletonize; finite-limit descriptions of coskeleta and exact sheafification identify the associated sheaf with K in every degree. Objectwise the resulting degree-n map is surjective, so the simplicial map is a trivial Kan fibration by the coskeleton lifting criterion. Its simplicial homotopy inverse induces a chain homotopy inverse on free R-modules. The free-R variant uses the same simplicial homotopy.

proof.text: Notation. For a presheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ write $R[\mathcal F]$ for the presheaf $V\mapsto R[\mathcal F(V)]$ of free $R$-modules and $R[\mathcal F]^\#$ for its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For a simplicial presheaf $M$ let $P(M)$ be the complex of presheaves of $R$-modules with $P(M)_k=R[M_k]$ and differential $\sum_j(-1)^jR[d_j]$, and $C(M)=P(M)^\#$ (termwise sheafification) the alternating-face complex of free $R$-module sheaves of the statement; $H_i(M)=H_i(C(M))$. Construction of $K'$. Let $K'_n\subseteq K_n$ be the image subpresheaf of $f_n$, $K'_n(V)=f_n(L_n(V))$. Let $U$ be the $n$-truncated simplicial presheaf with $U_i=K_i$ for $i<n$, $U_n=K'_n$ and the simplicial operators of $K$. This is well defined: an operator $K(\psi):K_n\to K_i$ ($i\le n$) restricts to $K'_n$; for $\psi:[n]\to[i]$ with $i<n$ and $x\in K_i(V)$ write $x=f_i(y)$ ($f_i$ is an isomorphism), then $K(\psi)(x)=f_n(L(\psi)(y))\in K'_n(V)$. So $U$ is an $n$-truncated simplicial subpresheaf of $\mathrm{sk}_nK$ with inclusion $\iota:U\to\mathrm{sk}_nK$, and $\mathrm{sk}_nf$ factors as $\iota\circ\phi$ with $\phi:\mathrm{sk}_nL\to U$. The category of presheaves of sets has finite limits, so by [lem-weil-pbc-truncated-coskeleton-finite-limits] (1) $K'=\operatorname{cosk}_nU$ exists and its counit $\varepsilon_U:\mathrm{sk}_nK'\to U$ is an isomorphism. By the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton] let $f':L\to K'$ correspond to $\phi$. Let $c_K:K\to\operatorname{cosk}_n\mathrm{sk}_nK$ be the canonical morphism, an isomorphism by hypothesis, and put $q=c_K^{-1}\circ\operatorname{cosk}_n(\iota):K'\to K$ with $\operatorname{cosk}_n(\iota)$ from [lem-weil-pbc-truncated-coskeleton-finite-limits] (3). Then $q\circ f'=f$: the morphisms $\operatorname{cosk}_n(\iota)\circ f'$ and $c_K\circ f$ into $\operatorname{cosk}_n\mathrm{sk}_nK$ both correspond to $\iota\circ\phi=\mathrm{sk}_nf$ (the first by the defining identity of $\operatorname{cosk}_n\iota$, the second because $c_K$ corresponds to $\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{sk}_nK}$), so they are equal. By functoriality of $C(-)$ and of homology, $H_i(f)=H_i(q)\circ H_i(f')$.

source.place: Lemma 01GD (lemma-acyclicity), proof, first paragraph, lines 679-689: 'we first let K_n' ⊂ K_n be the sub presheaf which is the image ... Denote K' = cosk_n U'

proof.text: $q$ becomes an isomorphism after sheafification in every degree. Degree $n$ of $\iota$: $K'_n\to K_n$ is a monomorphism of presheaves of sets, i.e. its two kernel-pair projections agree; sheafification preserves finite limits [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact], so $(K'_n)^\#\to K_n^\#$ is a monomorphism of sheaves. It is also an epimorphism, because its composite with $L_n^\#\to(K'_n)^\#$ is $f_n^\#$, an epimorphism of sheaves by the hypothesis that $L_n\to K_n$ is surjective after sheafification. Hence it is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-sets-mono-epi-iso]. In degrees $i<n$, $\iota_i$ is the identity. So the termwise sheafification $\iota^\#:U^\#\to(\mathrm{sk}_nK)^\#$, a morphism of $n$-truncated simplicial sheaves, is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-truncated-coskeleton-finite-limits] (2), (3) to the functor $\Phi=(-)^\#$ from presheaves to sheaves of sets, which preserves finite limits [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]: $(K')^\#=\Phi\circ\operatorname{cosk}_nU$ is an $n$-coskeleton of $U^\#$, $\Phi\circ\operatorname{cosk}_n\mathrm{sk}_nK$ one of $(\mathrm{sk}_nK)^\#$, and $\Phi\circ\operatorname{cosk}_n(\iota)=\operatorname{cosk}_n(\iota^\#)$ is an isomorphism since $\iota^\#$ is. As $c_K$ is an isomorphism, $q_m^\#:(K'_m)^\#\to K_m^\#$ is an isomorphism for every $m\geq0$.

source.place: Lemma 01GD, proof, first paragraph, lines 681-692: 'Assumption (2) means that the sheafification of K_n' is equal to the sheafification of K_n ... Because we can construct K'_m as a finite limit, and since sheafification is exact, we see that (K'_m)^# = K_m [read: K_m^#]. In other words, (K')^# = K^#'

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-sheaf-sheafify-first] applied to $q_m:K'_m\to K_m$, whose sheafification is an isomorphism by the previous step, $R[q_m]^\#:R[K'_m]^\#\to R[K_m]^\#$ is an isomorphism for every $m$. These are the components of the morphism of complexes $C(q):C(K')\to C(K)$ (they commute with the differentials because $q$ is a morphism of simplicial presheaves), so $C(q)$ is an isomorphism of complexes of sheaves of $R$-modules and $H_i(q):H_i(K')\to H_i(K)$ is an isomorphism for every $i$. It therefore suffices to show that $H_i(f'):H_i(L)\to H_i(K')$ is an isomorphism, where now $f'_n:L_n\to K'_n$ is surjective as a map of presheaves.

source.place: Lemma 01GD, proof, first paragraph, lines 692-697: 'We conclude, by exactness of sheafification once more, that H_i(K) = H_i(K'). Thus it suffices to prove the lemma for the morphism L -> K''

proof.text: Fix an object $V$ of $\mathcal C$; we show that $f'(V):L(V)\to K'(V)$ is a trivial Kan fibration [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. For $i\le n$ the counit identifies $K'_i$ with $U_i$ (it is an isomorphism, [lem-weil-pbc-truncated-coskeleton-finite-limits] (1)), and under this identification $f'_i=\phi_i$; so $f'(V)_i$ is bijective for $i<n$ ($\phi_i=f_i$) and surjective for $i=n$ ($K'_n(V)=f_n(L_n(V))$ by definition). The canonical morphism $K'\to\operatorname{cosk}_n\mathrm{sk}_nK'$ is an isomorphism: $\operatorname{cosk}_n(\varepsilon_U):\operatorname{cosk}_n\mathrm{sk}_nK'\to\operatorname{cosk}_nU=K'$ is an isomorphism by (3) of that node since $\varepsilon_U$ is, and it is inverse to the canonical morphism because both composites correspond under the bijection of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton] to the counits, hence are identities. The canonical morphism of $L$ is an isomorphism by hypothesis. Evaluation at $V$ preserves finite limits ([lem-weil-pbc-truncated-coskeleton-finite-limits] (4)), so by (2) of that node the canonical morphisms $L(V)\to\operatorname{cosk}_n\mathrm{sk}_nL(V)$ and $K'(V)\to\operatorname{cosk}_n\mathrm{sk}_nK'(V)$ of simplicial sets are isomorphisms. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-coskeletal-map-trivial-kan] applies to $f'(V)$, and it is a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Lemma 01GD, proof, second paragraph, lines 699-707: 'for any object U of C we see that the morphism of simplicial sets L(U) -> K(U) satisfies all the assumptions of Simplicial, Lemma 01A6. Hence it is a trivial Kan fibration'

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] there are $g_V:K'(V)\to L(V)$ with $f'(V)\circ g_V=\mathrm{id}$ and a homotopy $h:L(V)\times\Delta[1]\to L(V)$ from $\mathrm{id}_{L(V)}$ to $g_V\circ f'(V)$. Write $C_\bullet(S;R)$ for the free $R$-module chain complex of a simplicial set $S$; by definition $P(M)(V)=C_\bullet(M(V);R)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-homotopy-free-chain-homotopy], $C_\bullet(g_V;R)\circ C_\bullet(f'(V);R)=C_\bullet(g_V\circ f'(V);R)$ is chain homotopic to the identity, and $C_\bullet(f'(V);R)\circ C_\bullet(g_V;R)=C_\bullet(\mathrm{id};R)$ is the identity. So $C_\bullet(f'(V);R):P(L)(V)\to P(K')(V)$ is a chain homotopy equivalence and induces isomorphisms $H_i(P(L)(V))\to H_i(P(K')(V))$ for all $i$ (chain homotopic maps induce the same map on homology, the same node).

source.place: Lemma 01GD, proof, second paragraph, lines 707-713: 'In particular it is a homotopy equivalence (Simplicial, Lemma 08NS). Thus Z_L(U) -> Z_K(U) is a homotopy equivalence too'

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] (1) the homology presheaves are computed objectwise, so the previous step (for every $V$; the inverses $g_V$ need not be natural, only $f'$ is) shows that $H_i(P(f')):H_i(P(L))\to H_i(P(K'))$ is an isomorphism of presheaves of $R$-modules for every $i$. By (2) of the same node, $H_i(C(M))=H_i(P(M)^\#)\cong H_i(P(M))^\#$ naturally in $M$; sheafifying the isomorphism $H_i(P(f'))$ shows that $H_i(f'):H_i(L)\to H_i(K')$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 01GD, proof, second paragraph, line 714: 'This for all U. The result follows.' (with the exactness of sheafification as in Lemma 01GC, lines 656-660)

proof.text: By steps 1, 3 and 6, $H_i(f)=H_i(q)\circ H_i(f')$ is a composite of isomorphisms, for every $i$.

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks 01GD (hypercovering.tex 662-715), read with 01GC, Simplicial 0183/0185 (coskeleta as finite limits), 01A6 (coskeletal criterion), 08NL/08NS/08NM (trivial Kan fibrations), 019S/019Y (homotopies to chain homotopies) and Sites 00WJ/00WN, Modules on Sites 03AB/03AC. Steps: construct K' = cosk_n of the image truncation and the factorisation f = q o f'; q is a degreewise isomorphism after sheafification (mono+epi of sheaves, sheafification preserves the finite limits giving the coskeleton terms); hence the free R-module sheaf complexes of K' and K are isomorphic (03AC with R); objectwise f' is a trivial Kan fibration (01A6), so has a section that is a homotopy inverse (08NS), giving a chain homotopy equivalence of free R-module complexes (Mathlib SSet.Homotopy.chainComplexMap); homology presheaves are objectwise and sheafification commutes with homology. Statement kept (n >= 1 as stated; the proof works for n >= 0). Stacks writes (K'_m)^# = K_m where K_m^# is meant. Eight new nodes: three Mathlib leaves (sheaves of sets balanced; R-module presheaf sheafification exact; free chain homotopy from simplicial homotopy), a definition leaf (trivial Kan fibration = I.rlp), four unsplit (coskeleton finite-limit formula with preservation, 03AC with R, 01A6, 08NS). LeanSearch returned HTTP 500 throughout; recorded, with LeanFinder, Loogle and grep for each new node.
split_report.blueprint: The blueprint node lem-weil-pbc-hypercover-free-resolution proves exactness in its proof, first paragraph ('Exactness is a local assertion ... Thus every cycle is locally a boundary') by a local cone construction; the DAG's split of it replaces this by the Stacks coskeleton induction, of which this item is the inductive comparison step (its step 2, 'Thus [this node] identifies all free-module homology sheaves of K^n and K^{n-1}'). The steps here realize that comparison: steps 1-3 the passage to the image coskeleton (local surjectivity of the matching map, the blueprint's 'supplies a simplex with exactly those faces after an etale cover'), steps 4-6 the objectwise filling (the blueprint's cone/filling of simplices with given faces, here as the trivial Kan lifting) and the chain homotopy ('the alternating-face formula gives dh+hd=1').
